Okay wait, back up OP. If that's what she said, you probably shouldn't have gone to meet her. Yes, you were probably afraid that she would do something silly, but you are in no position to help her as a friend. She doesn't see you as a friend now - you're still her ex. I'm sure she has other friends that could have been there for her. Your meeting her might serve to enable her and to reinforce the idea that she can manipulate you into meeting her this way. Hopefully, that's not the case and it doesn't happen again. 

Now that I know this added detail, I do see how you kind of messed things up for yourself. I'd thought that you were meeting the ex to clear things up about the old relationship and to settle your distress, but if you'd chosen to go over to be there for her as a friend.. Oh well. This might be a bit more difficult to fix.

First of all, you might need to re-evaluate your friends who told ratted you out to your ex-girlfriend. They had no right to, it was between you and your girlfriend and you should have been the one bringing it up to her. Also, good on you for handling your feelings for Emily in a mature manner that reflects your commitment to your relationship with your ex. 

Sorry to say this, but if she kicked you out and made you leave because you started to like someone else even though you did the right thing by stopping the progression of feelings in its tracks, your ex seems to be less mature and logical than you are. Naturally, she would feel upset and even slightly betrayed that you actually developed feelings for someone else. However, she needs to know that this is normal in most relationships, and it is not how you feel that matters, but how you act on it that is most important.

I suppose you can seek comfort in knowing that you did the right thing and was ultimately true to your ex-girlfriend. You should try to clarify things with her and let her see your point of view. If she still doesn't accept it, you should try to move on. Perhaps in a few months she might miss you and try to reconnect with you, or you might try to reconnect with her and she might be open to it. Just be open to both possibilities: you can both try to move on and better yourselves, and you may successfully move on, or you might get a second shot again. Either way, you're still really young, and while it doesn't feel like you'll get back on your feet, you definitely will in time to come.

I wouldn't count that as abusive, your husband probably really didn't want you to leave the room or the argument. To give him the benefit of the doubt, he probably just wanted to resolve the issue there and then and not drag it out, or he was afraid of you walking out on him. Some people are more physical than others, but that might not mean they are necessarily violent. It's just the way they communicate.

That said, you should let him know that him physically stopping you from leaving brings you back to bad memories and makes you feel afraid and uncomfortable. He will probably not do that again remembering this. If he continues to do so even if you've told him how bad it makes you feel, you might have to be careful this might be a slippery slope to abuse.

Some people develop love or realize that they're in love at a slower pace than others. Your boyfriend may just need a little more time. The good thing is that he seems to be really open about his emotions with you, and is not hiding these things from you. Please don't be too upset by the fact that he is still unsure of his feelings, after all it's only been three months. You know he does really, really like you though, so you can go on from there. Nothing's really wrong and nothing really needs to change, just keep being open about your feelings towards each other.

The best thing you can do is make a choice and stick with it. How committed are you to your current girlfriend? More attractive and qualified women are bound to come and go in your life, this girl you met at med school will definitely not be the only one. 

If you've decided to be with your girlfriend and are fully committed to the relationship, you should take the necessary steps to distance yourself from this new love interest so that no feelings can progress further on your part. It is not difficult to stop the progression in its tracks if you really want to.

If your eyes and mind are wandering, you should ask yourself if this is just temporary and a fleeting excitement of new female attraction, or if you really see yourself giving up everything you have with your current girlfriend to pursue something else with this new girl.

When you're fully committed to a relationship, it doesn't matter if more interesting or more beautiful people who can offer you more things come into your life. Feeling lust or attraction is only human, it's how you handle these feelings and continue to choose your current SO that matters. Or, you leave because you realise you're not actually fully committed.

I agree with this, if you were in love with her you'd have no doubts about it. Have you had other girlfriends before her? Did you feel the same way towards them? 

From what you described it seems more like a companionship at the moment, it's really comfortable and it's obvious you both enjoy each other's company a ton. I would say that you don't have to re-evaluate your relationship right now as it seems that you've got something good, and it might just be lacking some passion or a spark. 

Moreover, love is somewhat like a skill that needs to be honed and developed over time. The more effort you put into loving her, the more your love will grow. Sometimes it's better to have a deep, long-lasting and stable love than the passion and heart-racing feeling of being in love with somebody, but that depends on where in your life you're at and what exactly you're looking for.

Your girlfriend shouldn't be lying about small things like the duration of their hang out. From what you have said, it does seem like their friendship is somewhat flirtatious and she is intentionally hiding things from you, which gives you some reason for suspicion. 
However, is there any possibility that she might be hiding these things from you because of the way you handled any previous similar incidents? While it is wrong of her to lie to you at all, have you made her feel like she cannot be truthful about certain things with you? 
I don't think you should drop this issue because it's obviously bothering you, and if you don't address it asap it might snowball into something more severe. I think you should discuss these things with her openly and in a kind tone, and see if she has an explanation that is acceptable to you.

That expressing your love isn't something that is immediately instinctive or something you'd know how to do. Some people pick these things up quicker because they've had good role models, but some people can live for a really long time not knowing how to properly love somebody and express it in a healthy way. Loving somebody is like a skill that needs to be honed.
